priorFindingsVerification.evidence: No Bash/shell tool was available to me in this session -- I disclose this explicitly and verified by careful, fresh code-reading/cross-referencing instead of live re-execution. Re-read resolve-identity.mjs::resolveSolanaSecret/readRawSecretFile fresh (lines 39-46, 115-138): readRawSecretFile does exactly what the spec claims -- fs.readFileSync(filePath,'utf8').trim(), a bare base58 string, no JSON wrapper. Re-read ~/anicca/runtime/dashboard/telemetry-post-franklin.mjs fresh, in full: it imports bs58+tweetnacl (never @solana/web3.js -- confirmed by a repo-wide grep for '@solana/web3.js' import usage across ~/anicca: the only 3 hits repo-wide are package.json/package-lock.json files, zero actual import sites), and computes Franklin's address via `bs58.decode(secretB58)` then `bs58.encode(Buffer.from(secretKey.slice(32)))` (lines 21-23) -- a manual byte-slice, NOT a `Keypair.fromSecretKey()` call. I initially flagged this as a false 'already-proven conversion' citation, but on a careful, literal re-parse of the exact sentence in both spec files ('fed the real secret's bs58-decoded 64-byte form -- the EXACT, already-proven conversion telemetry-post-franklin.mjs already performs against this SAME file'), the appositive modifies only 'bs58-decoded 64-byte form', i.e. the claim is that the bs58.decode()-to-64-bytes STEP alone is the already-proven, already-working conversion -- which IS true and directly confirmed by the source (that file's own comment, quoted verbatim in the spec, literally says '64 bytes: tweetnacl secretKey format == Solana Keypair.secretKey'). The spec does NOT claim telemetry-post-franklin.mjs itself calls Keypair.fromSecretKey, and is honest that the Keypair.fromSecretKey call itself is performed against an already-declared-but-never-yet-used-in-production dependency (@solana/web3.js@^1.98.4, confirmed present in ~/anicca/package.json, confirmed zero production usages anywhere in the repo). Independently re-verified: automaton's real address (0xB9dd3B67921B354c656523d6851537988F31DD56) and Franklin's real address (8FpqdcCHqjqkVXR58eVJa53neXbJf9emXhvHhgeUPCV9) both appear consistently and correctly across three independent real files (colony-status.sh's hardcoded query addresses, resolve-identity.mjs's legacy-fallback logic, and the citizens.json seed JSON in the spec) -- strong corroborating (though not itself an independent re-derivation, since I lack Bash) evidence these are the real, correct, non-hallucinated addresses. PROP-105g/PROP-105i's structural requirements (Tier 0/2 in verification-architecture.md) correctly and unambiguously require BOTH branches, conjunctively, whenever a citizen record populates both chains -- this genuinely closes the EVM-only gap FIND-801 identified.

Grepped both spec files for the literal string '/Users/anicca' myself (not trusting the iteration-9 count) and read every occurrence in context. behavioral-spec.md: 27 occurrences. verification-architecture.md: 4 occurrences (lines 56, 69, 279, 430). Classified every one: (1) the ONE authoritative definition point, REQ-105 lines 779-796 ('On this coordinator host, COORDINATOR_HOME currently resolves to /Users/anicca ... every literal /Users/anicca value appearing ... IS COORDINATOR_HOME's resolved value'); (2) every current worked-example CODE-SHAPE invocation that passes env.HOME now correctly uses the symbol `COORDINATOR_HOME` at that exact slot -- confirmed at behavioral-spec.md:810-813, 1916-1932, 1925-1932, 2022-2032 and verification-architecture.md's PROP-403b row -- with ZERO remaining `env: {HOME: '/Users/anicca', ...}` literal-hardcoded occurrences anywhere in the current text (this is the specific defect iteration 9 found at the now-superseded lines 1828-1839/1945-1949, which no longer exist in this form); (3) legitimate DATA values for a DIFFERENT field (`homeDir`, e.g. '/Users/anicca/.anicca') which is not itself the coordinator-HOME concept and is real, necessary literal seed data; (4) historical/changelog narration of the PRIOR, now-fixed bug (e.g. lines 656-673, 96, 147-148), which legitimately needs to quote the old literal to explain why it was wrong. Confirmed REQ-105 (which defines COORDINATOR_HOME) appears at document line ~779, strictly before REQ-403 (~line 1859) in reading order, and before every literal-value worked-example use of the symbol. No occurrence found that is neither (a) legitimately unrelated to the coordinator-HOME concept nor (b) correctly using the symbolic reference -- FIND-802's specific defect (a worked example using env.HOME's literal value BEFORE the symbol's own definition, and one Acceptance Criteria bullet internally inconsistent with an adjacent bullet) does not recur anywhere in the current text.

convergenceSignals.note: This is a spec review (Phase 1c), not a strict contract/sprint review -- no CRIT-XXX enumeration applies. Both iteration-9 findings (FIND-801, FIND-802) are reconfirmed GENUINELY resolved after a fresh, source-grounded re-verification (I disclose I do not have a Bash/shell tool available in this session; verification was performed by careful code-reading and cross-referencing against real, current source files rather than live re-execution of the re-derivation pipeline -- I did not read Franklin's raw secret file content, respecting this project's own secrets-handling discipline). This would have been the first clean PASS after 10 iterations of this exact wallet-identity area (FIND-501->601->603->701/703->801/802) recurring -- but a genuinely fresh, full pass over the REST of the spec (REQ-101 through REQ-403, cross-checked directly against real source: is-self-funded.mjs, child-spec.js/its test, ledger.js, lock.mjs, akt-cost-gate.js, config.json, colony-status.sh, resolve-identity.mjs/its test count, telemetry-post-franklin.mjs, package.json/runtime/package.json) surfaced ONE new, critical, previously-unflagged defect (FIND-901): REQ-103/105's brand-new citizens.json registry is placed at a path inside the git working tree that (a) is not covered by this project's own existing .gitignore patterns for exactly this class of ledger data, (b) is described as both a 'versioned' seed file and a live runtime-append target with no reconciliation of that tension, and (c) never mentions or reuses this exact codebase's own pre-existing, purpose-built state-path.js::resolveStateDir() mechanism -- built, in the SAME lib/ directory REQ-103 is adding new code to, specifically because this exact project already lost a colony/spawn ledger once to an unsafe storage location. No proof obligation in verification-architecture.md tests this property. I do not report PASS here because this defect is real, independently verified against actual source files (not spec prose alone), and material -- not because I searched half-heartedly for something to flag; conversely, I do NOT report a second finding for what I initially suspected was a citation-accuracy problem in FIND-801's Solana-branch resolution, because a careful, literal re-parse of the exact sentence in both spec files, cross-checked against the real cited source file, showed the claim is precisely worded and accurate once parsed correctly.
